title: Console cached query results and trace links resolve to previous API key after customer rotated API key
content:
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after rotating their API key, Console dashboards and ad-hoc usage queries continue to show results and trace links tied to the previous API key. Clicking trace links from the Console leads to 404s or traces attributed to the old key. This appears to be a cache/staleness problem on the Console/usage-analytics side where cache entries are not invalidated correctly after API key rotation.

Impact:
- Customer cannot reliably link dashboard query rows to live trace anchors (404s)
- Usage numbers in Console may temporarily reflect activity attributed to the old key instead of the new one
- High business impact for this enterprise customer due to audit/compliance reporting needs

Environment:
- Prod environment for BrightHealth AI (org: brighthealth-ai) in us-east-1
- Console version: web-2026.02.14
- Cache-service: redis-cluster-prod-3 (managed), cache-key-prefix v2

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Rotate API key via the Console > API keys > Rotate for org brighthealth-ai
2) Open Usage -> Ad-hoc Query with filter api_key: <new-key> and time range last 24h
3) Observe that panel rows still show request_ids and trace links for requests made with old key
4) Click a trace link -> Console opens trace URL and shows 404 or a trace page with request_id that predates rotation

Observed logs / snippets provided by customer:
- Example request_id seen in Console: req_20260309_7c9f3a8b
- Trace anchor from Console: trace-span-0a1b2c3d (resolves to old-key-owner)
- Customer-side API audit shows calls credited to new key from 2026-03-09T16:12:24Z

Attachments: customer-provided screenshots, session recording, and API audit CSV (uploaded to ticket).

investigation_notes:
03/10 - Triage by Support (Aisha): Verified customer repro steps in a staging replica. Confirmed Console is serving cached rows that include request_id/trace links linked to old API key after rotation.
03/10 - SRE (Diego): Examined cache key format in cache-service. cache-key included api_key_id in v1 but v2 rollout switched to org_id. Observation: rotation job updates api_key table but does not trigger cache invalidation for entries keyed by api_key_id in legacy caches. Some panels still reading from legacy cache prefix (v2 migration not complete across all pods).
03/11 - Eng (Sana, backend): Looked at request routing and link generation. Trace links are generated using stored request metadata pulled from the usage-analytics index. Indexing pipeline attaches original api_key_id as metadata; on rotation, a downstream migration job expected to remap historical entries but task hasn't completed and migration flag is off.
03/11 - Hypothesis: Two independent issues: (1) Console frontend sometimes reads from legacy cache prefix v1 which is keyed by api_key_id and remains stale post-rotation, (2) indexing migration that would remap historical requests to the org-level view hasn't been run for this customer's partition, so trace anchors reference old api_key values and the live trace lookup uses new key leading to 404s.
Relevant traces/logs: /logs/console/cache-debug/2026-03-10.log, /logs/indexer/migration-partition-42.log (partial failures)

actions_taken:
03/10 19:14 UTC - Support instructed customer to open an incognito session and re-run the query to rule out browser-level caching. Incognito showed same results.
03/11 02:32 UTC - SRE manually flushed legacy cache prefix for brighthealth-ai on redis-cluster-prod-3 (keys matching 'v1:org:brighthealth-ai:*'). This momentarily allowed new queries to surface correct request_ids for new key.
03/11 04:00 UTC - Engineering kicked off the per-org indexing migration job for partition 42 (affected customer). Job progress looked healthy but some records failed mapping due to legacy malformed api_key entries.
03/11 09:22 UTC - Added temporary console guard: panels will prefer live index read when an API key rotation event is detected in the last 24h, bypassing cache for affected orgs. Deployed as emergency feature flag rollout (ff/console/rotation-cache-bypass).
03/11 18:11 UTC - Notified customer of workaround and requested confirmation that trace links now resolve.
Customer confirmation 03/11 19:05 UTC: Reported that trace links are resolving for most rows but a small subset (approx 0.8%) remain 404ing.

comments:
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10T18:40Z: Created ticket after phone call with BrightHealth AI. Customer needs audit-aligned usage numbers by EOD 2026-03-12.
Diego Morales (SRE) 2026-03-10T20:05Z: I confirmed cache key mismatch; preparing safe flush plan for redis (will do per-org prefixes during off-peak windows).
Sana Reddy (Backend Eng) 2026-03-11T01:10Z: Index migration job has partial failures - some legacy API key records don't have a valid org_id. Writing a small remediation script to repair mappings for those records.
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-11T09:30Z: Enabled emergency feature flag to bypass console cache for orgs with rotation events. Not ideal long-term but reduces surface for 404s.
BrightHealth AI (Customer) 2026-03-11T19:05Z: Verified after guidance; majority of links correct now. Remaining few traces still 404; will attach examples.

workaround:
Temporary: Admin/Support flushed legacy cache prefixes for the customer's redis shard and enabled ff/console/rotation-cache-bypass which forces live index reads for orgs with an API key rotation in the last 24h. Customer can also add a dummy query parameter to bust console cache (e.g., ?bust=1) for ad-hoc queries until fix is rolled out.

root_cause:
During the api_key rotation rollout we migrated cache keying to org-level (v2) but not all console pods and the legacy indexing pipeline were fully migrated. Rotation does not trigger invalidation of v1 cache keys nor robustly remap historical usage entries that reference old api_key_id, leaving stale cache and index entries that generate trace links pointing to old key-scoped traces.

resolution_plan:
Short term: Complete per-org cache flush and finish the indexing remap and remediation script (Sana). Medium term: Update rotation workflow to emit cache-invalidation events and add automated migration verification (Diego/Sana). Add unit/integration tests to prevent future regressions. Deploy fix: patch indexing job to tolerate malformed legacy records and run migration across affected partitions (target: 2026-03-15).

resolution_notes:
03/12 - Partial remediation completed: cache flush and migration resumed; residual malformed records detected and repaired by remediation script. Feature flag left on for 48h monitoring. Engineering to run full verification across all enterprise orgs.

follow_up_tasks:
ENG-7123: Add cache-invalidation hook to api-key rotation service (assigned: Sana Reddy)
SRE-4409: Create safe per-org cache flush runbook and automate (assigned: Diego Morales)
OPS-2311: Run full indexing remap across partitions for enterprise orgs and validate trace link resolution (owner: Platform Eng)
DOC-1294: Update Console admin docs to document cache-busting and rotation impact (owner: DevEx)
SEC-502: Evaluate audit implications and notify compliance team if historical usage attribution changed post-migration
